subject: Peregrine — Inference stability incident / exec coordination
messages:
From: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@peregrine-fin.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Clarke <david.clarke@peregrine-fin.com>
Date: 2027-02-20T08:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Noticeable latency and transaction errors this morning

Rafael —

We started seeing a significant increase in latency and a spike in downstream 5xx errors around 07:45 UTC. Our payments pipeline that calls your /generate endpoint is timing out intermittently; throughput has dropped to ~40% of normal. Can you confirm whether there is an incident on your side and whether you can provide an ETA? We can provide traces if helpful.

This is impacting settlement windows for a small subset of our corridors (~5% of traffic) but it’s hitting high-value customers and the CFO is asking for an update.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Morgan
VP Product, Peregrine Financial
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@peregrine-fin.com>, David Clarke <david.clarke@peregrine-fin.com>
Date: 2027-02-20T08:20:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Noticeable latency and transaction errors this morning

Team —

Forwarding an urgent report from Peregrine. Key facts from their side:
- Latency: median p50 ~220ms -> current p50 ~610ms for the affected route
- Error rate (5xx): baseline 0.3% -> current ~8%
- Throughput: dropped to ~40% of baseline for ~5% of their traffic (specific corridors)

Immediate ask: Marissa/Jonas, can infra confirm whether any host pools or autoscaling activities correlate? Karthik, please check model variant fallback logs and prefix cache errors. Laura — coordinate comms and a short exec note. I’m copying the customer and CCing Evelyn for SLA/credits posture.

I’ll stand up a quick war-room (video + phone bridge) at 08:35 UTC. If you can’t make it, ping status in the thread.

Rafael
Director of Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@peregrine-fin.com>
Date: 2027-02-20T08:28:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Noticeable latency and transaction errors this morning

On 2027-02-20 08:20, Rafael Mendes wrote:
> Forwarding an urgent report from Peregrine. Key facts from their side:

We’re seeing elevated scheduling latency in the us-west pool starting at 07:42 UTC; autoscaler triggered a burst then failed to attach 3 nodes (API errors). Root cause appears to be a failed driver upgrade rolling out in the dedicated cluster that created transient GPU init failures — that caused request queuing on a subset of routing shards.

Preliminary impact: ~350k requests over the past hour routed to degraded hosts, KV cache misses increased (miss rate +17%). Model fallback triggered for some long-sequence requests which increased token-cost and processing time.

Taking actions now:
- Rolling back driver patch on the affected pool (in flight)
- Draining and replacing 6 nodes that fail health checks
- Flushing routing cache for Peregrine routes to force rebalance

I’ll post logs and the node list in the Jira ticket after rollback completes. ETA: 25–35 minutes for initial stabilization.

—Jonas
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@peregrine-fin.com>
Date: 2027-02-20T09:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Noticeable latency and transaction errors this morning

Thanks — quick update from runtime/model side:
- We observed model variant fallback for long-sequence requests (variant-b -> variant-c) which increased per-call compute by ~2.5x.
- KV cache saw a correlation: a malformed prefix key caused cascade cache misses for one tenant shard (Peregrine). Patch ready to prevent further malformed inserts.
- Trace sample shows a 5xx stack from a pointer deference in the inference runtime; a hotfix branch is prepared and ready to be promoted to the affected pools after Jonas’s rollback completes.

Planned steps (post-rollback):
1) Deploy runtime hotfix to drained nodes only
2) Promote patched nodes back into service with controlled ramping (10% intervals)
3) Monitor 5xx rate and p50 latency; have a rollback window of 15 minutes per ramp step

I’ll attach a short mitigation plan and the perf dashboard snapshot.

Karthik
Lead Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Peregrine — Inference stability incident / exec coordination

External update to Peregrine (sent 10:03 UTC):
Hi Alice / David —

Thank you for the prompt report. We have an active incident on a subset of our dedicated pool affecting some Peregrine traffic. Immediate engineering actions are underway (driver rollback, node replacement, runtime hotfix).

Current status (10:03 UTC):
- Impact: increased p50 latency (~610ms), 5xx ~8% for affected corridors, throughput degraded to ~40% for ~5% of traffic.
- ETA for initial stabilization: ~30 minutes
- Next update: 10:30 UTC or earlier if we have significant changes

We will provide a post-incident summary with root cause, timelines, and any customer credits if applicable.

Sincerely,
Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@peregrine-fin.com>, David Clarke <david.clarke@peregrine-fin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-20T15:03:00Z
Subject: Final update: Peregrine incident resolved — timeline and next steps

Alice / David —

Summary (final post-incident):
- Timeline:
  • 07:42 UTC — initial latency/error spike observed by Peregrine
  • 08:20 UTC — Redwood war-room mobilized (this thread)
  • 08:28–09:00 UTC — infra rollback of driver patch; affected nodes drained and replaced
  • 09:05–09:40 UTC — runtime hotfix deployed to drained nodes and ramped back in controlled intervals
  • 09:55 UTC — p50 latency returned to baseline (~210ms), 5xx back to <0.5%, throughput normalized
  • 10:30 UTC — internal verification complete; postmortem started

- Customer impact: About 2 hours total from first observation to full normalization for the small subset of corridors. High-value transactions were affected; we are prioritizing review for compensation/credits where appropriate.

- Actions taken: driver rollback, node replacements (6), runtime hotfix for malformed cache inserts and pointer guard, routing cache flush, and a controlled re-onboarding of nodes. Logs and node lists attached (logs_20270220.zip).

- Next steps for Redwood:
  1) Complete postmortem and share within 72 hours
  2) Push a permanent fix to prevent malformed prefix keys and a stricter canary for driver updates
  3) Engage Peregrine for any contractual remediation (EULA/SLA credits) — Laura and Marissa to coordinate

We apologize for the outage and will follow up with a root-cause write-up and remedial timeline. If you prefer a short executive briefing call, I can schedule one with our CTO and Head of Product this week.

Thanks for your patience,
Rafael Mendes
Director of Sales, Redwood Inference
(Attachments: proposed-mitigation-plan.docx)
